citations.assessment: The digital Bavli supports the father identification, nickname, three months on the road, and one day in the academy. It omits the explicit return duration and one day at home.
Rabbi Yochanan interprets Isaiah 58:2 to credit even one day of study in a year as a whole year.
Rashi gives an outbound three months, one day of study, and the return to his wife for Sukkot. The explicit lengths of the return journey and home stay in Heilprin require further collation.
The Bet heading points back to Idi as Yaakov’s father.
The Yod entry explicitly discusses the Chagigah figure and distinguishes him from a Shabbat narrative.

holds.raw: ובעין יעקב הגי' רב אידי בריה דרבי יעקב בר אידי
holds.reason: Keep the stated Ein Yaakov reading as Heilprin’s edition claim.
